# Ordinary deepest-face exhaustion and uniform vanishing of the physical buffer

This note proves the contributor's new actual body mechanism. At an ordinary local
minimum, the minimal base faces containing deepest bases must together cover
every sampled base. Otherwise enlarging one uncovered input fiber, followed
by taking the ACTUAL canonical hull, keeps the raw maximum depth fixed and
strictly increases the original mixed mass.

Applied to globally optimizing buffered pairs as epsilon decreases to zero,
this excludes a nonzero limiting physical parameter h=epsilon^(d+1)L.
The resulting vanishing theorem uses NO contact martingale, source weights,
finite-PL representation, cap regularity, or optimizer derivative. It does
not establish a Gamma payment or OC.

Archive distinction: exact depth isolation on a projection face is already
proved in Section 1 of
`candidate 25fed51eab0d77f0`.
It is recalled below as a dependency. The new step is the uncovered-input
expansion, followed by its use with the physical-buffer scaling.

## 1. Actual finite-family definitions and depth continuity

Let P be a finite base set, and let positive compact d-dimensional convex
fibers K_z, d>=1, be exactly the sampled fibers of

    C=conv union_(z in P) ({z} x K_z).

Set B=conv(P), S=union_z({z} x K_z), dm=sum_z dX|K_z,
M=sum_z |K_z|. The original raw depth D_C(p,y) is the infimum of dm(H) over
all closed ambient halfspaces containing (p,y). Define

    q_p=max_(y in K_p) D_C(p,y),
    Q=max_(p in P) q_p,    beta_0=Q/M,
    I={p in P:q_p=Q}.

When the base has rank zero (including n=0), set baseDepth=M as a formal
whole-base trace. There is no actual nonzero pure-base normal in that case;
all ordinary ambient caps used below have a nonzero continuous normal.

The maxima are attained. One direct continuity estimate will also be useful.
Suppose actual finite families K'_z approach K_z in Hausdorff distance on
the same P and have a common continuous-coordinate bound. Let

    Delta=sum_z |K'_z symmetric_difference K_z|.

If y' approaches y at the SAME base p, then

    |D_(C')(p,y')-D_C(p,y)|<=Delta+A |y'-y|,            (1)

where A is a common bound for the sum of maximal continuous section areas.
For d=1 use one per interval; in general bounded fibers lie in a fixed ball,
so every unit-normal (d-1)-section has a common finite area bound.

To prove (1), tighten each containing cap to pass through its mark. For a
nonzero continuous normal normalize its Euclidean norm to one. Moving y to
y' shifts its threshold by at most |y'-y|, independently of the base tilt;
the added continuous slab costs at most A|y'-y|. Changing the fibers at a
fixed halfspace costs at most Delta. Pure-base caps select the same finite
base traces and change mass by at most Delta. The comparison is uniform over
all normals, including unbounded base tilts, so infima preserve it.

Positive-body Hausdorff convergence gives Delta->0. Approximating marks in
both directions by Hausdorff-close points now proves continuity of every q_p,
of Q, and of beta_0. On one fixed family the same estimate gives continuity
of D_C in y, including its boundary, and hence the asserted attainment.

## 2. The archived exact face-depth identity

For any face F of B, let S_F contain just the sampled fibers with z in F,
with the RESTRICTION of the original measure. Then for every mark over F,

    D_C(p,y)=D_(S_F)(p,y).                             (2)

Restriction makes one inequality immediate. For the reverse expose F by a
base affine functional l which is zero on F and strictly negative on the
finitely many bases outside F. Extend any relative face cap to an ambient
affine cap {A>=c}. Adding T l to A leaves every closed trace over F unchanged.
For sufficiently large finite T it excludes every other compact sampled
fiber exactly. Its ambient normal can be chosen nonzero; at most one T could
annihilate a chosen extension. Thus every face cap is realized with exactly
the same raw mass in the full family. Infima prove (2), including all boundary
atoms and pure-base caps. For F=B the statement is tautological.

The identity does not require a minimizing cap to be attained, and it does
not supply a mass/parity inequality by itself.

## 3. New actual expansion when a deepest-face union misses a base

For p in B let F_p be its minimal containing face. Suppose there is a base

    u in P outside union_(p in I) F_p.                 (3)

For t>0 enlarge ONLY the input fiber at u to K_u+t Ball_d. Keep all other
old input fibers and define the actual body

    C_t=conv[ ({u} x (K_u+t Ball_d))
                 union union_(z!=u) ({z} x K_z) ].     (4)

Use ALL the actual sampled fibers K_z(t)=(C_t)_z afterward. This is not an
assertion that the other fibers outside selected faces remain independent.
They may enlarge as required by convexity. The projection stays B; if P was
lattice-complete, no new integer base is introduced. The canonical hull of
these new sampled fibers is exactly C_t.

Every sampled fiber satisfies the explicit inclusions

    K_z subset K_z(t) subset K_z+t Ball_d.             (5)

For the second inclusion express a point of the new hull using one point
from each input fiber and base barycentric weights. Replace the changed input
point in K_u+t Ball_d by an old point within t. The old convex combination
belongs to K_z by actual compatibility, and the new combination moves by at
most lambda_u t<=t. Thus all fibers converge in Hausdorff distance, uniformly
over the finite P. Also

    M_t>M for every t>0,       M_t->M,                 (6)

since K_u(t) contains the strictly larger positive body K_u+t Ball_d and
every other fiber only enlarges.

For p in I, condition (3) says u is outside F_p. The face property implies

    C_t intersect (F_p x R^d)=C intersect (F_p x R^d).  (7)

Indeed a convex combination whose projected base belongs to F_p uses only
inputs with bases in that face; the only changed input is outside it. Hence
every sampled fiber on F_p is EXACTLY unchanged. Equation (2) gives

    D_(C_t)(p,y)=D_C(p,y) for all y in K_p,   p in I.  (8)

For every p outside I, its old fiber maximum has a strict gap q_p<Q. There
are finitely many such p. Continuity from (1) and (5) therefore keeps every
one below Q for all sufficiently small t. Equations (8) then give the exact
raw maximum, not merely a first derivative:

    Q(C_t)=Q(C),       beta_0(C_t)=Q/M_t<Q/M.           (9)

This is a legitimate arbitrarily small compatible descent of normalized
ordinary depth.

**Minimal-face exhaustion theorem.** At every ordinary local minimum with
respect to actual compatible fixed-base Hausdorff perturbations,

    P subset union_(p in I) F_p.                      (10)

No differentiability, supporting-facet allocation, or polytopality is used.
In particular, if P contains a relative-interior base of B, some ordinary
deepest base must be relative-interior: no proper face contains that base.
The theorem does not claim that every deepest base is interior, or that the
faces in (10) have disjoint mass or parity sets.

## 4. A positive physical buffer strictly raises every interior depth

This strictness can be proved without attained buffered caps. Let Y=(p,y)
be own-interior, let Gamma be any positive definite norm on continuous
covectors, and give its caps a fixed displacement delta Gamma(u), delta>0.
Pure-base cuts remain unchanged. Write D_delta(Y) for the resulting depth.
Then

    D_delta(Y)>D_0(Y).                                (11)

First the exact finite-family bound from the companion stratification note is

    D_0(p,y)<=baseDepth(p)-|K_p|/2.                    (12)

For clarity, in positive base rank take a minimizing pure-base cap through p,
{a.(z-p)>=0}. In rank zero use the formal a=0 and baseDepth=M; the two ACTUAL
caps in the following argument still have continuous normals +u and -u and
are nonzero. At
large finite base tilt the two continuous perturbations +u and -u capture
strictly positive bases fully, strictly negative bases not at all, and
complementary parts of every boundary-base fiber. Their masses sum to
2 baseDepth(p)-V{z:a.(z-p)=0}<=2 baseDepth(p)-|K_p|.
At least one gives (12). Continuous hyperplane boundaries have zero d-volume.

Choose an own ball B(y,r) subset K_p and normalize Gamma(u)=1. Then ||u||<=C
for a fixed C. EVERY nonvertical buffered cap through Y contains its ordinary
through-Y cap plus the disjoint own-ball strip

    {-delta<=u.(X-y)<0} intersect B(y,r).

This strip has a uniform positive volume, for example

    c=vol_(d-1)(Ball_(d-1)) (sqrt(3)r/2)^(d-1)
                                     min(r/2,delta/C)>0,       (13)

with vol_0=1 for d=1. It follows that every such buffered cap has mass at least
D_0(Y)+c. Every pure-base cap has mass at least
baseDepth(p)>=D_0(Y)+|K_p|/2 by (12). Taking all infima proves

    D_delta(Y)>=D_0(Y)+min(c,|K_p|/2)>D_0(Y).

No strict proper-base gap, minimizing direction, or regular coarea is assumed.

## 5. A fixed limiting buffer cannot coexist with an ordinary minimum

Let C be an ordinary local minimum as in Section 3. Let h>=0 be a finite
sampled-concave full-space parameter, positive or zero on each fiber interior,
and use the physical displacement

    delta_h(p,y)=[h(p,y) E_(K_p)(y)/M]^(1/N)

times a positive covariance norm Gamma(u), with boundary displacement zero.
Suppose this buffered family's maximum is the SAME raw Q as the ordinary
maximum. Then h is zero on every sampled fiber.

To prove this, an ordinary deepest mark has positive raw depth and is
own-interior. Positivity follows from an inner ball; at a sampled boundary
point a continuous support normal of its own fiber extends by the finite
base support LP to a support plane of the whole canonical hull, whose outer
cap has zero mixed volume. If h were positive at that deepest mark, (11)
would make its buffered depth exceed Q. Thus h vanishes there. Nonnegative
concavity on a positive fiber implies that an interior zero forces h to
vanish on that ENTIRE sampled fiber.

Let Z be the zero-fiber set. If p in Z, every sampled base in F_p is also
in Z: p in relint F_p can be expressed as a convex combination with positive
weight at any chosen z in F_p, and nonnegative concavity would otherwise
give a positive interior value in the p-fiber. Thus all F_p for ordinary
deepest p are contained in Z. Exhaustion (10) gives P subset Z, as claimed.

Equivalently, if h were nonzero on some sampled fiber, choosing u outside Z
in (4) would leave every ordinary deepest face unchanged and contradict the
ordinary local minimum. This argument uses no parameter stationarity or
transport representation.

## 6. Uniformly vanishing physical parameters at joint global buffered minima

Now use the genuine normalized bad-body compactness and limiting closed-minor
quotas of the attained-minimum framework. Fix the base P and dimension d, and
let beta_0^* be the global ordinary infimum over its actual positive compatible
families. Suppose beta_0^*<Gamma_d/k and EXPLICITLY assume the established
compact positive bad-sublevel and limiting quota framework. In the intended
application P is the canonical cardinality-minimal bad base; badness of an
arbitrary fixed P alone would not imply these extra hypotheses. The original
minimal-bad-base theorem then supplies compact positive normalized
representatives and the limiting quotas (1) of
`candidate 36607dd22d2fb045`.

For epsilon_j down to zero choose globally minimizing, or o(1)-optimal, joint
body/positive-concave-log-parameter pairs (C_j,L_j), in the same full parameter
class. Assume their values tend to the joint infima; exact attainment is a
special case. Let beta_j be their buffered normalized maxima. Then

    beta_j -> beta_0^*.                                (14)

The lower bound beta_j>=beta_0^* holds because buffering only enlarges each
cap. For the upper bound fix ANY ordinary near-minimizer C_ref and choose the
admissible L=1. On this fixed body the buffer is O(epsilon), uniformly in
marks and unit continuous normals. The all-direction slab bound gives
beta_epsilon(C_ref,1)<=beta_0(C_ref)+O(epsilon). First let epsilon tend to
zero, then let the ordinary reference error tend to zero. This proves (14)
without presuming an ordinary minimizer or differentiating either optimizer.

For all large j the pairs lie below one fixed b<Gamma_d/k. The proved bound
in Section 2 of the companion stratification note applies to
h_j=epsilon_j^N L_j. Its proof uses only these compact bodies, the limiting
minor quotas, and b<1/k; it does NOT use the source certificate. Thus h_j has
a uniform sampled upper bound. Canonical concave-roof compactness gives a
subsequential sampled interior limit h>=0. The energy vanishes uniformly at
moving sampled boundaries, so the physical buffers converge uniformly to
[h E/M]^(1/N) Gamma even without boundary convergence of h_j.

The all-direction comparison (1), with this additional uniformly convergent
threshold displacement, makes the limiting buffered maximum beta_0^* by
(14). On the other hand

    beta_0^*<=beta_0(C_j)<=beta_j,

and ordinary depth continuity from Section 1 gives
beta_0(C)=beta_0^* for the compact limiting body C. Thus C is a GLOBAL ordinary
minimum and the limiting buffered maximum equals its ordinary maximum.
Section 5 forces h=0 on all sampled fibers.

This proves the uniform assertion for the whole sequence:

    max_(z in P,X in K_(j,z)) epsilon_j^N L_j(z,X) ->0. (15)

Indeed if a sampled maximum stayed above eta>0 on a subsequence, pass to the
compact limit just considered. In that fiber an old uniform inner point g
satisfies max h_j<=(1+R/r)h_j(z,g), by positivity and concavity. A positive
maximum therefore forces a positive interior limiting value, contradicting
h=0. Finiteness of P permits a fixed fiber subsequence.

Since energies, masses, and covariance norms are uniformly bounded on the
normalized family, (15) also gives UNIFORM VANISHING of every actual physical
buffer displacement for unit continuous normals. The assertion is about
sampled fibers, or a bounded canonical sampled-roof representative. Arbitrary
concave extensions can have irrelevant unsampled bumps and are not covered.

## 7. Exact scope and remaining obligations

The body mechanism is an exact finite compatible expansion, not an independent
motion at an interior fiber or a formal first-order support change. It keeps
the ORIGINAL raw depth fixed before comparing original total mass. The
epsilon-limit proof relies on global optimization of the joint values (or
o(1)-optimal values) and the original compact bad-sublevel/quotas framework.
The local-minimum body statement allows the full actual fixed-base class. If
one works with mass/covariance-normalized representatives, the small expanded
body can be returned continuously to that normalization by reversible common
continuous-fiber affine maps, which preserve ordinary normalized depth.
It does not claim (15) for arbitrary fixed-body parameter optimizers, safe
families, or arbitrary prescribed positive weights; their known escape
calibrations are unaffected.

The conclusion removes nonvanishing physical-buffer escape in this specific
joint limiting setting. It supplies no convergence rate, no bound on L_j,
no uniform derivative of a parameter, and no Gamma payment for a physical
response. All supporting-facet and variational payment questions remain
separate. Full OC is not proved here.

## 8. Exact actual interval calibration of the finite descent

Take P={-1,0,1} and centered intervals of lengths 8, 9/2, and 1. They are
compatible: the middle interval is precisely the Minkowski average of the
endpoint intervals. Their total mass is 27/2. The endpoint fiber maxima are
4 and 1/2 by face isolation. At the middle center, every nonvertical through
cap has own mass 9/4, and its endpoint contribution has infimum 1. Indeed
for a slope a the endpoint contribution is

    clamp(4-a,0,8)+clamp(1/2+a,0,1),

whose minimum over the real line is 1, attained for sufficiently large
positive a. Opposite continuous orientations give the same infimum by
reflection. Pure-base caps cost at least 11/2 and do not bind. Reflection
of the entire family in the continuous coordinate makes depth even on the
middle fiber; convexity of each raw-depth superlevel implies its maximum
is at the center. Hence q_0=13/4 and the unique deepest BASE is -1, with Q=4.

Expand the middle INPUT by t[-1,1], 0<t<3/4, and take the actual hull. The
endpoint fibers stay unchanged and the middle length becomes 9/2+2t, still
compatible. The identical all-slope calculation gives

    q_0(t)=13/4+t<4,
    Q(t)=4,
    M_t=27/2+2t,
    beta_0(t)=4/(27/2+2t)<8/27.

This is the exact finite raw-plateau descent of Section 3. It is not a bad
counterexample or a strict-minor-quota calibration: the largest endpoint
violates its singleton quota. The general body lemma does not require that
quota; quotas enter only the separate compact limiting application.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_deepest_face_exhaustion_descent_defect_transport.py`
passes 755 exact checks: all slope breakpoints, the displayed finite identities
at rational t, and the rank-zero cap convention. It is a calibration, not a
replacement for the all-dimensional expansion or compactness proofs.
